item.tome02_page05.text: Do not forget to immediately start a fire. Food prepared over a fire is much better for satiating hunger. If your fire goes out, you most likely just need to add some more firewood. This is also the case for Smelters as well as other devices that require fuel to function.
item.tome02_page06.text: To keep from starving to death, collect berries and the meat of wild animals. However, your surest course of action would be plotting out a garden and planting it with leek seeds. Peasants might have seeds, though little of their peaceful selves will remain in them. You'll make quick work of them, though.
item.tome02_page07.text: You cannot forget that you are surrounded by hundreds of monsters more dangerous than poor peasants. Turned by the Decay, Knights and Templars, too, have lost their minds! You will need weapons and armor to fight them. These can first be made of copper. Search for it in rocky places.
item.tome02_page08.text: A torch is not the most fearsome of weapons, but don't dare leave home without one. If night comes while you are away from home, a torch is your only hope. Remember, fire is the soul of Light, and your only salvation.
item.tome02_page09.text: Not everyone has forsaken us. Those who have their own interest in the Plaguelands frequently use us as their tools. But there are those who help us from the good of their hearts. To contact them as quickly as possible, assemble a cage for ravens. Doing so will make your life easier and open new possibilities.
item.tome02_page10.text: You will, of course, need several devices to refine lumber and stone, smelt ores, and weave cloth. You can build all of them with your own hands so long as you are capable of holding an axe.
item.tome02_page11.text: The province is stained with swamps, but their water is undrinkable. To keep from dying of thirst, build a well. Fill all the flasks you can find, for leaving home without water is risky—I'd even say bordering on madness.
item.tome02_page12.text: With time, however, you will learn to twist rope with the help of tanning racks, prepare leek soup on campfires, and even forge nails. There are no lackeys nor servants in the Plaguelands. A noble person must themselves look after their own well-being.
item.tome02_page13.text: There are even rarer items, which cannot be gathered or crafted. Do not forget to loot corpses, even the most homely object can be a treasure in the Plaguelands! And always keep an eye out for birds. Flocks of crows can often direct you to places from which you might profit.
item.tome02_page14.text: If you're lucky enough to find a dungeon map, do not hurry to go there. Yes, there are rumors that the treasures hidden away in dungeons are worth any risk, but a wise person will always take time to prepare. Before everything else, I speak of weapons, armor, food, water, and healing tinctures.
item.tome02_page15.text: From time to time itinerant merchants wander into our land. Desperate people... you can barter with them for prized valuables like weapons or rare crafting materials.
item.tome02_page16.text: When setting off for a long venture, always take a spacious sack for trophies and spare weapons with you. If your sword breaks in battle, it could mean your life.
item.tome02_page17.text: Beware of other Exiles. Desperation pushes people to shameful acts, and in the Plaguelands men are the most fearsome of monsters. I am running out of ink, but if you are still alive and reading my notes, it must mean you have some knack for survival. I think you can cope with the challenges of fate without my bothersome advice...
item.tome02_page18.text: This is the best day I've had since finding myself in the Plaguelands. Early in the morning I found a small Direwolfling. There were no adult wolves around and I decided to take the cute little furball to my castle. He's still really small, but I get limitless joy from watching him grow and become stronger.
item.tome02_page19.text: I built a suitable pen for him. It's enough space for one wolf, but yesterday I heard the whining of another wolfling. I guess the Direwolves are starving this year and leaving the weakest of their young to their own fate. So, before their food replenishes, I'm going to upgrade my pen to make it more comfortable and so I don't have to constantly trip over them in my home.
item.tome02_page20.text: These Direwolves are proving to be loyal and helpful companions. The most important thing is how many useful skills they can learn. I've reared about two dozen wolves and even bred a few. For now, Mathilda joins me on my adventures while Johan and Wilhelm guard my home from uninvited guests. And a few of my wolves are even helpful around the house.
item.tome02_page21.text: I've been intensively breeding for months now. At first, it seemed unpredictable—but I've identified a few patterns. It turns out wolflings can have a variety of coats as well as be predisposed to different skills. Why am I so concerned with all this? I want to know: how self-aware, how conscious can these pets become?
item.tome02_page22.text: Dear friend, if you ever come across a lonely wolfling—take it with you. A wolf is more than company on a dark night, they can be a friend for life. Yes, you have to make sure your pen has food and water, walk them and keep them fit—but there is no greater fulfillment than rearing a suckling pup into a battle-hardened wolf.
item.tome03.name: Origins of the Pestilence
item.tome03_page01.text: From the archives of the Scarlet Angels: after the emergence of the Gray Decay, studying its nature and origins has become one of our main occupations. On par with guarding hospitals and saving those Damned who have not lost their mind under the strain of the disease. Despite all this time that has passed, we still endeavor to find a cure to save all those who we can.
item.tome03_page02.text: When our Order first heard news of the epidemic which struck one of the imperial provinces, we thought it was another ordinary disease. It became clear only later that the Gray Decay does not kill but rather turns people into something altogether inimical to the Creator's Light. It is no surprise that those who lost their minds became a weapon in the hands of heathen wizards. It was clear that cults of Darkness were at work.
item.tome03_page03.text: Not all our scouts returned from the Plaguelands. But we did understand somethings. Our observers believe that the province was struck by the pestilential emanations of the Plague God—one of the ancient heathen gods, whose cult had suddenly enjoyed a surge of popularity across the Empire's provinces. We are not certain yet, but our suspicions are strengthened every passing day, and we continue to keenly observe in the name of the Light and for all those who depend on our defense.
item.tome03_page04.text: To feed the corruption, servants of the Plague God bring victims to their wicked master. The Emperor's warriors or locals not succumbed to the disease often become their victims. Places for such sacrifices are often called Soulmarks or Places of Power, for this is where the servants drain the lifeforce from their captives. To this day, coming across such places, one can hear the voices of those taken in the name of the Plague God.
item.tome03_page05.text: The souls trapped to Soulmarks are the subject of extensive study for the Order. Some of them scream out curses, others whisper secrets hidden from the living. But there are certain Places of Power, where a traveler might find safety from the Night Guest—an evil spawn of the Plaguelands. We believe that these Places trap the souls of those who, to their dying breath, kept faith in the Light.
item.tome03_page06.text: Though it is difficult to say this, but the emergence of the Plaguelands was not without treachery. Eyewitnesses assert that they saw warriors in the colors of one of the Empire's Orders in the province's forests not long before the epidemic struck. It was only later that our brothers-in-arms' treason became evident. The reasoning behind their actions, however, remains a mystery to this day.
item.tome03_page07.text: Aside from the traitors, there were righteous people amongst us, too. True warriors of the Light who the Plague God's priests destroyed to please their lord. But even in death, they continue to serve the living. After discovering a Fervent Place of Power, Exiles may pay homage to the fallen hero and receive a temporary blessing. They can direct the power given to them by the Light against the dark's filthy spawn.
item.tome04.name: Inhabitants of the Plaguelands
item.tome04_page01.text: Compiling the knowledge gathered by the Order's brothers on the Plaguelands, we stumbled upon the question of classifying the creatures now inhabiting the afflicted province. The first such classification was written by the Captain-Commander Jacques Kerr. According to his work, there are many a creature which cannot be counted either among humans or animals.
item.tome04_page02.text: Exiles are persons touched by the Gray Decay. Their nature is little studied. There are conflicting opinions about their origins and their powers. They are rarely encountered outside the Plaguelands. The Emperor's Edict decrees the destruction of all touched by the corruption. But by the secret command of our Order's master, our brothers escort the wretched souls to the Plaguelands. May the Light have mercy upon them.
item.tome04_page03.text: The dire wolf is an ancient beast, preserved by the heathens to protect their forests and hunt for imperial scouts. They are much larger than normal wolves and forever hungry, for they must compete for meat with the Damned.
item.tome04_page04.text: Lepers are peasants or townspeople afflicted with the Gray Decay. Their bodies and souls have been disfigured, their minds destroyed. They are insane now, attacking anyone capable of withstanding the disease. Servants of the Plague God use these unfortunates as living weapons against imperial forces.
item.tome04_page05.text: The Damned are Lepers, reanimated after death. At the start of the epidemic, Lepers were buried like the other dead. But what later dug itself from the grave froze many an innocent with fear. There is no one to bury the wretches now, but many Damned still wander the Plaguelands. The Damned are considered to have lost all their senses and are the Gray Decay's final phase.
item.tome04_page06.text: Damned Knights are Imperial warriors who voluntarily accepted the Plague God's pestilence in return for the immortality of their souls and greater physical power. The consciousness of these monsters is under question. Our only reliable knowledge of them is their insatiable desire for human blood and suffering, which bring the plague warriors indescribable rapture.
item.tome04_page07.text: Damned Templars are the wicked foil of Harat's temple guards. They are knights of the Imperial Orders who voluntarily accepted the Plague God's pestilence in return for the immortality of their souls and greater physical power. They spread death and terror across the field of battle, delighting in the death throes of their enemies.
item.tome04_page08.text: Wailing Witches are widows, grieving their husbands, whose torment souls are permanently trapped by the Gray Decay. Wailing Witches find peculiar solace in serving the Plague God. If you hear a witch's cries from a distance, it's much safer to go around her than risk disturbing such a dangerous creature. You also shouldn't fall for her tricks: a witch can lure careless travelers into a trap before attracting all the surrounding Damned with her frenetic screams.
item.tome04_page09.text: The Night Guest is a demon who appears at night to drink the blood of the living. No mortal can kill the Night Guest, but fire can force him to retreat for a time. In addition, the Night Guest always avoids certain Places of Power—presumably because of the emanation of a large number of souls.
item.tome04_page10.text: Leprous soldiers are the Forsaken Order's foot soldiers. They've reached such spiritual and bodily decay that they show no sensation for anything around them, only obeying their commanders' orders. The Forsaken Order's soldiers are ready to kill anyone who has not accepted the Plague God's curse.
item.tome04_page11.text: The Possessed are captives of the Forsaken Order, reborn after their deaths. The bodies of those sacrificed to the Plague God sometimes revive. Possessed are predictable, but they wield the power and stubbornness of a wild animal. Unlike the Damned, who live above ground, the Possessed do not see the sun, which causes their skin to turn pale.
item.tome04_page12.text: A Forsaken is a knight of the Order of the Crushers, who voluntarily turned to evil. In according with their consecratory ritual into the Crushers, each Forsaken knight killed several of their brethren in arms who either did not wish to betray the Empire or who were too weak to be part of the new Order under the Plague God's standard.
item.tome04_page13.text: A Desecrator is a former Templar of the Order of the Crushers who swore allegiance to the Plague God. Their fanaticism and cruelty in the name of their lord make the Desecrators an example for their evil brothers in arms. They are the backbone of the Order of the Crushers. Anyone who comes across the Desecrators will either be turned or destroyed.
item.tome04_page14.text: Plague Spawn are servants of the Plague God, spreading the Gray Decay, infecting everyone they can reach. Their touch is not only poisonous, it is abominable.
item.tome04_page15.text: Fanatics are adherents of the Plague God, ready to sacrifice themselves to defeat their master's enemies. Seeing an enemy, fanatic will rush them—not to hug them—but to light a barrel full of explosive powder. The closer the explosion, the higher the chance no armor will save you.
item.tome04_page16.text: A Forsaken Hermit is a forgotten wanderer. Some veteran Forsaken are too sick to serve their Master, so they leave their brotherhood, hoping to earn the Plague God's auspices alone. Once a traitor—always a traitor, which means that you can learn all the Order's dark secrets from them. A dead Hermit is a silent one, however, so you need to figure out a way to get him to your Castle alive...
item.tome04_page17.text: Furious Desecrators are the Forsaken Order's elite warriors. Powerful fighters, they draw strength from their fury and wickedness. Every battle makes them stronger, every scar—more deadly. When they suffer heavy wounds, they only become more dangerous, striking more critically at their enemies. Though, no one has survived an encounter with them to confirm that.
item.tome04_page18.text: Plague Bandits are thieves, deserters, and runaway convicts who made it to the Plaguelands. Many of them are pagans with no sense of honor and who do not understand the fate they doomed themselves to by accepting the Plague God's corruption. They will do anything to survive, including cutting the throat of any stranger they come across.
item.tome04_page19.text: Some believe that the Dark Hunters are Exiles who have forsaken the light, joining bandits and brigands to steal from their former companions in misfortune. Others assert that they are former archers of the imperial army. Only one thing is for certain: if you can't fight them in a melee, then their arrows will cause serious problems—especially if you aren't wearing strong armor.
item.tome04_page20.text: Plague Barbarians are pagan tribal warriors who have long threatened the Empire's borders. In battle, these savages depend on their superhuman strength and large numbers. We were fortunate enough to scatter their large army in the northern lands of Lubenia. But even the splintered forces that remain in the forests and hills still present a deadly challenge to any lone Exile who happens upon them.
item.tome04_page21.text: Dire bats are wild creatures that rapidly attack tired travelers from the air. Nosediving, bats rip at their prey until it loses consciousness or too much blood. Without question these creatures of the Dark are of a supernatural origin and we have yet to understand their true nature, having killed but a few of the beasts with crossbows.
item.tome04_page22.text: Damned Inquisitors are former vanguard knights who have cut all ties with their previous orders and have been led into madness. They kill only to satisfy their thirst for blood. Despite the corruption of their souls, these warriors have not lost an ounce of their fighting skills or fearlessness, and some can even defeat a brother of the Order in single combat.
item.tome04_page23.text: The Northern Lands are full of dangers, but they are also a treasure trove for those courageous enough to explore them. There are those, however, who prefer to work covertly. One clear example is the Greedy Hoarder—an odd being, too repulsive to be human but also too agile for a leper. The brothers of the Order only encountered the Hoarder twice—and we know almost nothing about him. Though not violent, he's a conniving thief who keeps everything he can scrounge or scavenge in a humongous sack. Rumor says it's brimming with rare items. We haven't, however, been able to catch the Hoarder yet to see if the rumors are true.
item.tome04_page24.text: A Mourning Reaper's Shadow is an otherworldly entity that was once a knight of the imperial Mourning Reapers Order. Shadows drain the lifeforce of their victims and can temporarily become invisible and invulnerable to any weapon. They inhabit the ruins of the Sinister Citadel in the northern lands.
item.tome04_page25.text: Vargs are a new breed of direwolves created by the Plague God's acolytes through the use of alchemical potions and dark rituals. The predators' fangs drip with a poison so deadly it can kill Exiles in a matter of minutes.
item.tome04_page26.text: Virbjorns are resurrected werebears. Some believe these monsters serve the Nameless God, but their corrupted nature leaves space for doubt.
item.tome04_page27.text: Not all the Gray Decay's victims were properly buried. At the height of the epidemic, corpses were unceremoniously thrown into mass graves without any rites or rituals. No one could have imagined what a mistake that was. The corrupted bodies have grouped into hordes of mindless monsters. Attack one of the spawn and another is sure to appear.
item.tome04_page28.text: The Damned Squire is a fervent servant of the Forsaken Order's commander. Stripped of his free will and sanity, he will spill his enemies' blood until ordered to stop by his master. He attacks with heavy objects in an attempt to immobilize opponents to stop any chance of escape or resistance.
item.tome04_page29.text: Plaguis are the next stage in the evolution of plague monsters, with deadlier poison and stronger bodies. They can easily be distinguished by their red skin and repugnant smell.
item.tome04_page30.text: The Black Knight is a veteran Forsaken warrior, a survivor of many battles. His armor is darkened from the soot of burned villages and the blood of his enemies, slain in the name of the Plague God.
item.tome04_page31.text: The Plague Commander is one of the officers of the Forsaken Order. As strong as several warriors, he can momentarily become enraged when entering combat and rip practically any opponent in half.
item.tome04_page32.text: The Bloody Reaper is a powerful spirit of Shobol, summoned from beyond this world. His phantasmal essence is soaked in the blood of martyrs, giving him the power to draw strength from two worlds simultaneously. The Bloody Reaper's arrival is the first sign of the coming end of the world.
item.tome04_page33.text: Sufferers are unfortunate captives tormented through rituals honoring the Plague God. Excruciating torture disfigured their bodies and broke their minds. When there is nothing left in Sufferers except pain and hatred, the Torturers release them into the dungeon for sport, setting them on one another and uninvited guests.
item.tome04_page34.text: Axe Throwers are barbarian hunters and servants of the Plague God. Do not mistake their bloodlust for recklessness. These enemies prefer ranged combat and will try to keep a distance from their prey so long as it is still alive.
item.tome04_page35.text: Slaughterers, once knights of the War Dogs Order, are now terrifying killing machines. Driven by a desire to kill, victims' screams are music to their ears. The few survivors of encounters with these servants of the Plague God say that their master has gifted them with immortality.
item.tome04_page36.text: Unlike witches, Priestesses are trained to serve the Plague God from a young age. In the barbarian lands whence they came, they are revered as soothsayers. They convey their God's will to chosen warriors, prophesizing the great deeds, glory, and riches that the future holds for them. The Priestesses themselves take part in battle, showering their opponents with poison darts. For this reason, they try to keep their enemy at a safe distance.
item.tome04_page37.text: The Torturers are the mighty soldiers of the once renowned order of the War Dogs. Bloody rituals have warped their minds and endowed them with immense strength. In an attempt to become even more powerful, the Torturers are willing to maul the flesh of not only enemies, but allies as well. Although their fury may seem self-destructive, do not expect an easy victory. In battle, a single Torturer is worth a dozen ordinary knights.
item.tome04_page38.text: Fenrir is the Gatekeeper's new Direwolf. This beast is trained to track down those marked by the Plague God: the Exiles. Be on your guard if you decide to face Fenrir—his claws and fangs contain a deadly poison.
item.tome04_page39.text: A Horde Leader is a horrible spawn of chaos, all but consumed by madness. They say they were once Exiles who eventually succumbed to the plague. It's hard to say by looking at them—the damnation erases all signs of who these creatures once were. Horde Leaders are smarter and more aggressive than other enemies, and they have a pack of the damned at their beck and call.
item.tome04_page40.text: The Summoner knows the words in the half-forgotten barbarian language that will bring the most horrific forces into this world. He conducts bloody rituals to bind the shards of cursed souls together, subjecting plague-stricken creatures to a single will. On the Priest's orders, he collects material to create leaders for his army of the damned for eternal service to the Plague God.
item.tome04_page41.text: The Plague Priest Takhal is famous as one of the most dangerous priests of the north. For the barbarians who worship the Plague God, he is lord, commander, and prophet. When Takhal arrived in Lubenia, monster attacks became more frequent and organized, and now corpses and ruined homes grow more and more common in our lands.
item.tome04_page42.text: Headhunters are crafty and cautious enemies. Only the most experienced warriors from the barbarian tribes are given this honorary title after proving their skill in tracking down and restraining two-legged prey.
item.tome04_page43.text: Torturer Scouts are the eyes of their tribe. They watch everything that goes on around their camp ground and inform the priests. But that doesn't mean that they'll hesitate to attack any enemies they come across and gain themselves glory.
item.tome04_page44.text: Executioners who offer up innumerable victims to the Plague God earn his blessing and become Punishers, meting out destiny to the weak. They do not fear death, for their resurrection only makes them stronger.
item.tome04_page45.text: Torturers are pain factories, but the Cruel Torturer lifts the suffering of lower beings to new heights. When he fights, he grows more enraged with each injury he receives, and every blow he lands dampens the will to resist, even in the noblest of enemies.
item.tome04_page46.text: A Fire Guardian is a creature created in the chambers of the Torturers. It was once human, but has no recollection of that now. Its fury towards all living beings is immeasurable, and the durability of its natural armor means it can ignore attacks from regular weapons. Only cold deals significant damage to it.
item.tome05.name: Legend of the Emperor
item.tome05_page01.text: Three centuries ago, the continent was divided into many small kingdoms, constantly at war with one another. At that time, the Kingdom of Dagria—now known as the Capital Lands—was ruled by the glorious King Robert III, famous for his military valor and wise governance.
item.tome05_page02.text: In those days the religion of Harat grew in strength in the kingdoms nearest Dagria. Preachers told people of the defeat of Darkness by the Light and promised adherents a better life after death. The cult of Harat was persecuted and oppressed for a long time by evil heathens. For the followers of this new religion believed in one god and declared all the rest demons.
item.tome05_page03.text: King Robert saw in this an opportunity to expand his royal power and lead his people into the Light. He negotiated with the High Priests of Harat and declared theirs the only legal religion in his realm. King Robert erected a magnificent Temple in the capital and began pursuing wicked heathens across all of Dagria. In those days the priests proclaimed the king an agent of God on earth and declared his right to rule the entire world.
item.tome05_page04.text: Relying on the support of the priests and local adherents of the cult of Harat, Robert III—in just a few years—conquered the kingdoms of Falves, Kadesh, Lubenia, Birn, and became protector of the Teorsk Marches, thereby establishing the Eternal Empire of Light and declaring himself the first Holy Emperor.
item.tome05_page05.text: But prosperity did not last long. The government's strength was undermined through war, and the priests, having tasted power, demanded more privileges. As a concession to the hierarchs of Harat, the Emperor was forced to give his assent for the creation of an inquisition, which was completely controlled by the priests and punished any blasphemer or criminal against the faith.
item.tome05_page06.text: Once, the Emperor saw how the Inquisition tortured a beautiful woman accused of witchcraft and heresy. The Emperor was young and ordered them to release the witch. Kayla (as the witch was called) promised him dominion over the heathen tribes if he took her as his wife. The Emperor understood that the priests of Harat, who declared him their patron, would not dare make speak of such a relationship with a witch.
item.tome05_page07.text: The Emperor asked the witch to call to his side the otherworldly powers she served. Kayla prophesied that the Emperor would rule the entire continent, but he would have to fulfill his side of the deal. The Emperor promised to make the witch his wife, and she gave birth to a son. The boy was so handsome and strong that people could not look at him long without shedding tears of joy.
item.tome05_page08.text: When the boy turned one year old, the witch demanded the Emperor establish three knighthood orders to destroy other heathen kingdoms. The first order were the "War Dogs." The order was comprised of the strongest warriors from the peoples conquered by the Empire. Vicious berserkers struck terror into their enemies by just appearing on the field of battle. No army in the world could withstand them when the warriors, screaming their battle cry, crashed into their enemy's formation like an avalanche.
item.tome05_page09.text: The second order were the Twilight Riders. They were recruited from the western nomads, voluntarily in service to the Emperor. Wherever the Twilight Riders appeared, enemy ranks broke under the hooves of quick and bloody charges. The Riders, meanwhile slipped away like water, reforming and charging from where they were least expected.
item.tome05_page10.text: The third Order—the Dusk Blades—were known for their cruelty. And they were then not unreasonably called the Dusk Executioners. This Order was made up of former convicts and those sentenced to death. Those strong men, used to spilling blood on city streets, quickly quelled the dissent of any rebelling province.
item.tome05_page11.text: The new Orders proved insurmountable in war and allowed the Emperor to greatly expand the Empire's borders. The influence of Harat simultaneously grew within the country and beyond its borders. The ruler of the Empire of Light could not publicly marry a wicked witch. Doubts ate away at the Emperor's soul. After all, the king had bent to the priests' will to do away with the witch and secretly sent a temple assassin after her.
item.tome05_page12.text: Before her death, Kayla cursed the Emperor, promising that he would soon die a terrible death and his empire would fall, "When the Imperial family has two sons, the younger will swallow the older, and Death will sit on the throne." In fear, the Emperor refused to leave the palace. He surrounded himself with guards and priests. He elevated the witch's killer to be Master of a new order. Such was the origin of the fourth order: The Black Crows.
item.tome05_page13.text: The Black Crows were the most secretive and clandestine of the imperial orders. There were many legends about them. Some said that they were the throne's assassins. Others asserted that the Crows sought out and destroyed vile pagan relics and the most dangerous heretics. One way or another, they played a decisive role in the fate of the whole Eternal Empire of Light.
item.tome05_page14.text: Despite it all, six months after the witch Kayla's murder, Emperor Robert III died a gruesome death. His remains were found in the Emperor's bedchamber, and no one knew what had happened to him. The throne passed to Robert and Kayla's son, Darion I. But priests of Harat ruled as regents in the young boy's name. That was the end of the legend of Robert III Lightbringer, First Emperor of the Eternal Empire of Light.
item.tome06.name: Chronicle of the Eternal Empire
item.tome06_page01.text: In the seventh Year of the Descedent Light, by the bountiful Creator's mercy, King Robert III was declared the anointed, defender of the faith, and the First Emperor of the Eternal Empire. His rule was marked by countless glorious victories and the conversion of many people's to the true faith and heavenly mercy. Coming to his final rest in the thirty-seventh year of the Descent of the Light, Robert III Lightbringer left the throne to his only son, Darion I.
item.tome06_page02.text:
From the temple archives:
 "Taking into account the nonage of Emperor Darion, in its greatest wisdom, and with endless love towards the people of the empire, the High Council of the Priests of Harat has taken upon itself the great burden of governing the Empire in the name of the Light and for the sake of saving people's souls from corruption and other evils."
item.tome06_page03.text: In the forty-second Year of the Descedent Light, the High Council of Harat founded the order of the "Emperor's Shadows" to safeguard the sovereign from heathen evildoers. The order was comprised of the most zealous followers of the Emperor's cult—persons who wouldn't think twice about laying their lives down for Him and for the good of the Light and the Eternal Empire.
item.tome07.name: Legend of the Grim King
item.tome07_page01.text:
Three centuries passed since its creation, and the Empire founds itself at the peak of its power. The throne, at that time, was occupied by Emperor Wilhelm I, a 14-generational descendent of Robert the Lightbringer.
For three centuries now the priests of Harat had pulled the strings behind many Emperors and spoke in their name. But the populace loyally believed that they were led by the Emperor himself, and those with any doubts preferred to stay quiet, lest they fall afoul of the Inquisition.
item.tome07_page02.text: The Inquisition had power in every sphere of life. By order of Grand-Inquisitor Marn, three Great Orders were established to fight heresy. The Mourning Reapers became the sixth Imperial Order. They brought terror to any heretics and apostates across the Empire. The Order drew its number solely from the Zakkarites, members of a secret fanatical sect who professed contempt for pain and fear in the name of redemption for their sins and attaining bliss in the afterlife.
item.tome07_page03.text: The seventh order, the Iron Wolves, recruited from the uncivilized tribes most recently converted to Harat, who hoped that their new god would bring them military glory and bounty. The tireless and selfless warriors soon won the respect of friend and foe alike. Their act of heroism on behalf of the empire and faith quickly became legendary.
item.tome07_page04.text: The eighth Order was recruited from professional witch hunters and the Empire's most famous duelists. Later it accepted into its ranks graduates of the military academies, educated in the way of revering the Emperor's perfection. The brothers of this Order did not fight in ranks but rather served as hounds, tracking spies and the Empire's most secret enemies, no matter where they tried to hide. The Emperor's Heralds brought judgement to heretics in the name of their ruler.
item.tome07_page05.text:
Wilhelm I was vainglorious. As a young man he wanted to distance the priests from the throne. He disbanded his retinue of Emperor's Shadows, as their loyalty lay with the Harat faith, and surrounded himself with the Golden Guard, assembled from the Empire's best warriors.
The priest tried to reason with the ruler, claiming that the Empire would collapse without their protection. But the Emperor politely declined their every claim and took away the faith's right to speak in his name.
item.tome07_page06.text: To strengthen his grip on power in the Empire, Wilhelm I established four more orders, obedient only to him and impervious to the priesthood. The order of the Scarlet Angels were the embodiment of the Emperor's mercy. Wearing scarlet cloaks, they were the guards of hospitals and defenders of the common folk in times of war. Their selflessness and humility made them holy warriors in the eyes of the people.
item.tome07_page07.text: The Emperor's generosity was, in turn, impersonated by the order of White Shields. The order's brothers defended castles, fortresses, and roads across the empire. Fortitude, bravery, and fidelity to duty were the essence of the Shields in their white cloaks. Their reinforcement of ramparts immediately raised the spirits of any town's defenders, providing them with redoubled strength to fight in the name of the Emperor.
item.tome07_page08.text: The Imperial Lions are the inflexible embodiment of the Emperor's will. It is the most highly-disciplined Order, in which each knows their place and is prepared to carry out an order at any cost. The Empire's best commanders are the Order's officers, which is why the Lions have fought gloriously to victory  in many a hopeless battle, where any other Order would have suffered inevitable defeat.
item.tome07_page09.text: The Order of the Crushers was conceived as the embodiment of the Emperor's patience and guile. The Crusher's specialty became the capture of the enemy's most impregnable citadels. This Order's brothers were not keen to come face-to-face with their foes. Well-planned tunnels, destructive explosions, and giant trebuchets were their signature. Wherever walls fell, one could find these inventive warrior-engineers.
item.tome07_page10.text:
For years, the Emperor's authority grew immensely. The inquisition even came under his control, and the priests didn't dare contradict their sovereign. There were no omens of misfortune until the Emperor's concubine gave birth to twins. Wilhelm was not superstitious, but the priests reminded him of the prophecy concerning two sons in the imperial family and the fall of the Empire.
Wilhelm limited himself to just sending away one of the twins to a far off castle.
item.tome07_page11.text: Some outraged priests conspired against the Emperor. It took them many years, but in the end the Emperor was poisoned. He was succeeded by the "older" son, Ioann I. The boy was only twelve when, pressured by the priests, he agreed to have his brother murdered. The inquisitors ordered a young priestess in the service of the prince to cut his throat. But the priestess fanatically believed in the holy inviolability of the imperial family and couldn't complete her task.
item.tome07_page12.text: Taking the boy with her, the priestess ran to the pagan-infested forests of Lubenia, which stretched past the Empire's borders. The pagans they met did not kill them but rather took them in. The pagans, it turned out, retained the rites of a nearly-forgotten religion. After learning the evil truth about the cult of Harat, the priestess accepted the Dark faith of her ancestors and took a new name. They called her Aissa, meaning "preceptress" in an ancient tongue.
item.tome07_page13.text: Aissa became the young prince's foster mother, the only mother he knew. She was the only light in his life as the memories of his treacherous father and brother poisoned his mind. To receive the power for revenge against the Emperor and priests, the prince agreed to go through the ritual to accept the God of Death.
item.tome07_page14.text: The ritual was so horrific that even the pagan mages who brought it about were terrified of what they had done. Many days the prince felt his body slowly corrupting without dying, but when the ritual ended, the dark god gifted the prince powers unobtainable for mortals. So the prince gave his name to the Nameless God and he was consecrated to Death. The Great Darkness filled his inhuman heart.
item.tome07_page15.text: The boy grew up and forcefully subjugated many heathen tribes, making them his loyal slaves. There were rumors that his body was immortal and his soul filled with such an abysmal darkness that it threaten to swallow everything whole. With the aid of heathen warlocks and apostate priests, the pretender's army invaded the Empire and set towns and temples ablaze. That was when the Empire first heard of the coming of the Grim King, as the leader of the barbarians was called by the Harat priests.
item.tome07_page16.text: The Imperial Orders paid dearly to defeat the Grim King's army and chase him back into Lubenia's forests. The priests of Harat captured the Grim King, brutally murdered his stepmother, and only after pinning his body down with sacred seals did they perform an exorcism. The priests failed to extricate the Darkness from his soul. They could only shatter it into a thousand pieces, depriving the king's soul of the power it was bestowed by the Nameless God. His followers' souls also shattered into pieces.
item.tome07_page17.text: But that was not the end of it. Lubenia's forests became cursed places, abandoned by even heathens and heretics, where people didn't dare go come dusk. Few ever returned alive from a night in the forest, and the shadows which people spoke of only in hushed voices gave birth to the legend of the Night Guest - an immortal monster that hunts humans to drink their blood and abduct their souls.
item.tome08.name: History of the Treason
item.tome08_page01.text: With the ascendance of Emperor Ioann I to the throne, popular unrest increased year after year. More and more uprisings occurred across the whole Empire. Heresy raised its ugly head. Some said that the armies of heretics were led by demon-possessed heathen kings, who wanted nothing but the destruction of the Harat religion and to topple the young ruler from his throne.
item.tome08_page02.text: The most powerful heretical cult became that of the Plague God, who gave his followers odd pleasures and destroyed the flesh and minds of his enemies. The cultists themselves often turned into sore-ridden monsters, but they accepted this with enthusiasm as a blessing from their god. Wrath, pain, and terror brought them such bliss that they often disfigured their own bodies.
item.tome08_page03.text: The most ardent warrior against heresy became the Master of the Order of the Dusk Blades, Lord Marcus. His feats were legendary. However, upon visiting the same forest where the Grim King had been defeated, the ancient evil caught him, too. After one of many campaigns into the forests of Lubenia, Lord Marcus returned possessed by demons. He fought insanity for a long time, but it was a greater challenge than even he could handle. Driven by ghostly voices he sowed the first seeds of heresy among the Imperial Orders.
item.tome08_page04.text: Meanwhile, Darkness loomed on the edges of the Empire. Pestilence came from Lubenia's forests and swiftly spread to all the Empire's new provinces. At first, people thought that it was a plague epidemic, but the disease turned out even more terrifying than the black death. The infected lost their sanity and turned into monsters, hunting those who had not yet been touched by the disease. Darkness plunged it fangs deep into the flesh of the Eternal Empire of Light.
item.tome08_page05.text: Later, during the inquisitional trials, witnessed said that they saw warriors in the colors of the Order of the Black Crows in the forests of Lubenia before the outbreak of the Gray Decay - but no one had believed them then. Following their interrogations, witnesses one after another either succumbed to the pestilence or disappeared from their cells despite the doubled guards and depth of the cells underneath the capital temple.
item.tome08_page06.text: When the pestilence appeared, Lord Marcus seemingly awoke from a dream and started acting decisively. The first legion to fall were the War Dogs. Traitors from the Order mixed a potion given to them by Lord Marcus into their master's wine, and Master Karn went into an unrestrainable rage. Defeating many imperial servants and priests, he led his legion into the Plaguelands, where he joined ranks with the Damned, fighting against the Emperor.
item.tome08_page07.text: Rivers of blood were spilled. The Emperor sent his best warriors to stop the Darkness and defeat the heretics and apostates hiding in the Plaguelands. The Twilight Riders were the first to counter-invade Lubenia. Their sweeping offensive forced the heathen armies to stumble and then retreat deep into the forests. Many of the Plague God's priests were killed and thousands of Damned bodies were burned.
item.tome08_page08.text: But even thick forests and deep swamps could not stop the Emperor's will. Columns of Imperial Lions already marched along the roads liberated from the enemy armies. Division after division marched under the forests' canopies. The ringing of clashing blades rose across the province as it mixed with the war cries of imperial knights and the death cries of heretics.
item.tome08_page09.text: Only the frantic counterattacks of the Torturers—as the traitorous War Dogs now called themselves—could slow down the advance of the Emperor's best troops. The long battle continued day and night. Fresh troops replaced the fallen while the wounded were carried to the rear, and the battle continued with a renewed vigor. At some point a combined operation between the Imperial Lions and Twilight Riders crushed the Torturers and sent them retreating into the deepest, darkest forests.
item.tome08_page10.text: With sword and fire, imperial soldiers cut their way through hordes of enemies, but when victory was close and Lord Iven, Master of the Lions, was decisively crushing Karn's berserkers, cutting his way to their leader, the troops of two other Imperial Orders marched onto the battlefield.
item.tome08_page11.text: The beleaguered, wounded Imperial Lions and Twilight Riders raucously cheered the Dusk Blades as they formed up for battle. Behind them soldiers in Black Crow colors marched in line, crossbows at the ready. From there, the battle ended quickly and was one of the most mournful pages in the Empire's history.
item.tome08_page12.text: The Dusk Blades attacked the unsuspecting Imperial Lions from the back, splintering their formations and mercilessly destroying their demoralized opponents. The Black Crows rained bolts down upon the Twilight Riders instantly depriving them of their decisive mobility. The Imperial forces were crushed within an hour. The Master of the Twilight Riders, Peregrin Plag, was taken prisoner by the Black Crows, and Lord Iven went missing in action.
item.tome08_page13.text: The remnants of the Imperial Lions were scattered and many succumbed to the pestilence. Under torture, Peregrin Plag agreed to trick the warriors of his Order into a Black Crow trap, where they were surrounded. Threatened with being turned into mindless Damned, the Twilight Riders took an oath of allegiance to the Plague God.
item.tome09.name: History of Prince Luther
item.tome09_page01.text: When news broke of the simultaneous defeat of several imperial orders, the Emperor's son, Prince Luther, received his father's blessing to create a new order. The Prince was young, desired glory, and he found companions just like himself. The order recruited only the younger sons of nobles and skilled mercenaries. No one knew then that the seeds of corruption and pestilence had already started to sprout in his soul.
item.tome09_page02.text: Just a year after founding the order, which he named the "Imperial Sons", Prince Luther headed the second crusade into the Plaguelands. This time, they planned to destroy the remnants of the traitorous orders in one fell swoop and then retreat, not entangling themselves in a fight with the pagan natives. The Prince was joined by Lord Ingmar and his order the Emperor's Messengers, as well as Gerhard Eisenborg with the Order of the Crushers.
item.tome09_page03.text: The Imperial forces attacked the traitor's camp from their march, and the battle seemed to be leading to the enemy's complete destruction, but the entire crusade turned out to be an elaborate trap. The Plague God's promises had already lodged deep in Luther's and his companion's hearts. The corrupted and pleasure-seeking youths easily accepted the Plague God's gifts, betraying the empire and the whole of mankind.
item.tome09_page04.text: Attacking the Crushers from behind, the Imperial Sons sowed chaos in their ranks, destroying their battle readiness. The corner Crushers surrendered to the mercy of their victors. The Imperial Heralds kept their formation, retreated, and left Lubenia. Lord Ingmar could not bring himself to attack the Prince. That is how another, the last, crusade into the Plaguelands ended in catastrophe - a catastrophe from which the empire could not recover.
item.tome09_page05.text: To isolate the Plaguelands, the Emperor ordered the Order of White Shields to build a chain of fortresses around the forests of Lubenia and defend them day and night. Ioann I ordered the Scarlet Angels to search the Empire for outbreaks of pestilence and destroy every Damned they encountered. But filled with a sense of justice, the Scarlet Angels spared the damned who still had their minds - believing that so long as a person's soul fought with the pestilence there was still hope for them.
item.tome10.name: Commander Rin's Report
item.tome10_page01.text: For Lord Huginn's eyes only: My Lord, another step of our plan is successfully concluded. The new priest was exactly the person who could direct the energies of our restless ally in the right direction. Who would have thought that the northern barbarian could be so convincing. I don't know how he specifically reassured the Forsaken, but Master Eisenborg always listens to his advice.
item.tome10_page02.text: As we planned, none of the Forsaken would dare surface without permission from the master's new advisor. Eisenborg himself gave the priest the keys from the dungeon and declared him the order's Gatekeeper. We no longer have to worry that the Forsaken will repeat their individual attempts to attack the imperial forces or scatter about the forests, in which case it would take weeks to reassemble their forces.
item.tome10_page03.text: Turning the Forsaken into faithful soldiers of the Plague God is going according to plan. It looks like they have not noticed the changes happening to them, and I hope that will remain the case. In case of unforeseen issues, a battalion of heathens is camped past the river and awaits the priest's orders to invade the province.
item.tome10_page04.text: The only major possible obstacle to our plans might be the Scarlet Angel battalions. My people are doing everything they can to distract and confuse their scouts, but even the best sometimes fail. I'm also attempting to recruit some of the exiles living in the region, but it's too early to predict the success of that endeavor.
item.tome11.name: A Forsaken's Diary
item.tome11_page01.text: Our disastrous defeat has greatly changed the order. Our illusions of obligation and honor, which we held ourselves to before, have entirely disappeared. Lord Eisenborg has given into apathy and refuses to see anyone. The officers rounded up the remaining dregs of our order and relocated us under the ruins of an old temple. It's a dismal, depressing place, but it's better than staying the forests among the mindless and soulless Damned.
item.tome11_page02.text: No one wanted to join the dark gods' side, but there's no path for us back into the Empire. The Emperor has ordered the execution of anyone touched by the Plague God's breath. And that means the inquisition's dungeons, torture, and death in the cleansing flames is all that awaits us back home.
item.tome11_page03.text: We did not forsake the Empire, before that the Emperor forsook us. Master Eisenborg says the Emperor himself is to blame for our current situation, and we are in the right to unleash our anger upon the soldiers still loyal to him - to fight and win back our right to return home from our undeserved exile.
item.tome11_page04.text: Black crows no longer appear in our camp above the ruins. In their stead has appeared a most evil-looking barbarian. He speaks impertinently with the master and is not afraid to use force against anyone standing in his way. Between his giant height and animal strength it's doubtful that anyone would risk fighting him.
item.tome11_page05.text: Master Eisenborg has changed considerably. Blood sacrifices have started. First it was runaway peasants and the occasional exile. But when some of the officers tried to get the master to see reason, he started sacrificing his own knights. "Cleansing," as the Gatekeeper calls it, happens every day, and I am beginning to fear for my life.
item.tome11_page06.text: The priest killed brother Manse today. Light knows, the poor man didn't deserve it. But the barbarian spares no one and kills everyone who even looks at him wrongly. The priest is strong—no one can stand against him. The madness that's gripped the order is only becoming worse, and we are delving deeper into an abyss.
item.tome11_page07.text: The changes touching this order are becoming more apparent. I can now feel how my body is beginning to transform. Every day I am stronger than the last, and the pains racking our bodies this whole time have become so familiar that no one pays attention to them anymore. Perhaps the master was right, and the Gray Decay has another side—one that we will experience for ourselves.
item.tome11_page08.text: My thoughts are muddled, and I cannot remember much from before our crusade into the Plaguelands. But that is not important. I am transforming, and I enjoy it more every passing day. I killed a brother yesterday who wanted to take my weapons. Though he pretended to sleep, I could see how he conspired to steal my sword and dagger.
item.tome11_page09.text: The Plague God's gifts are incredible. I once could not have imagined that I could wield such power. I thought our master had gone mad when he ordered us to sacrifice our brethren who failed to convert to the Plague God. But, in truth, it is the rest of the world that has gone mad, fooled by those priests of Harat.
item.tome11_page10.text: The Plague God guides us. The Plague God transforms us. The Empire must die!
item.tome12.name: The Journal of Gerhard Eisenborg
item.tome12_page01.text: Our former allies' attack took us by such surprise that my warriors had no chance of resisting them. The imperial ideals we served to protect were desecrated. The old world was destroyed. Critically injured, I was immobilized and captured by the Black Crows. I still remember the piercing cold gaze of their captain. He looked at me as though I was a lifeless corpse.
item.tome12_page02.text: A few warriors picked me up and dragged me for a long time. Eventually I found myself in a hut with an altar. The Crows hid after throwing me to the feet of a heathen priest. He muttered something under his breath, but when the apparitions pierced my consciousness, his voice rang loud and clear. I saw what awaited my order. I felt the pain and terror of the coming transformation of my brothers into evil beasts barely resembling humans.
item.tome12_page03.text: It seemed like my pain would last forever and the terror would grow until my mind shattered into madness. But suddenly, through the agony, I heard His voice, "The Empire is nothing. Human life is fleeting. Bring me your people and you will learn the very meaning of life. Humans come and go, but life goes on. Changing and gathering strength, life defeats death." And then I blacked out. But death did not come to take me.
item.tome12_page04.text: I was let go that same day. Half blind and deaf I wandered through the forest and by some miracle stumbled upon a camp of our Crushers. They were spared, but none there felt relieved. The warrior's faces and bodies were covered in spots. The Gray Decay touched us all. What I saw in the priest's hut came back to me over and over again in nightmares, but I fought them back. Honor dictated I care for my people and keep them from dying in that wretched place.
item.tome12_page05.text: Two days my shattered order limped back to the border of the Plaguelands, but when we made it out of the darkness of the forest, we were met with a rain of arrows. Knights in the colors of the White Shields stood in rank and prepared to throw us back. Unprepared and unwilling to fight out brethren, we left. The Emperor made an edict that anyone touched by the plague was to be executed. Our fate was sealed.
item.tome12_page06.text: After a long trek through the Plaguelands, losing many brethren either to the plague or to the monster they transformed into, we found respite beneath the ruins of a temple, burned by heathens. Grief fills my heart. We have nowhere to go. We have neither strength nor a purpose. We can only pray to the gods for mercy. The only question is which one of them might answer our prayers in this forsaken place.
item.tome12_page07.text: When the Crows came, internally, we had already agreed to serve the Plague God. At worst only death awaited us, or something worse than death—transforming into evil beasts, hungry for flesh. My people deserved a better end. Today I swore an oath to do everything I can to save the remnants of my order. Or at least the ones who still have faith in my word.
item.tome12_page08.text: The Crows brought a priest. The heathen quickly interested us with his preaching. He told us of the Plague God's wonders, of his power and wisdom. He explained that change is the purpose of life, that we shouldn't fight for some phantom, heavenly Light—but for earthly life. Life as it already is—chaotic and indomitable in all its forms and manifestations.
item.tome12_page09.text: That day, we forsook the Emperor and Empire. We became the Forsaken. And all who did not wish to join the new order we sacrificed to the Plague God. The more offerings we brought to our god, the more our power grew. My power. A long time has passed since I last felt myself a normal person—I have become something greater, something more perfect.
item.tome12_page10.text: We did not choose our fate. It was chosen for us. We did not betray the Empire; the Empire betrayed us. We sent envoys to parlay. We begged, but were answered with arrows, death, and dishonor unbecoming of our lives of faithful service.
item.tome12_page11.text: They think we forgot. They think we forgave. But one day we will be strong enough to take revenge upon the Empire for its betrayal. They will feel our pain and terror. Our former brethren will see the true power of the Plague God.
item.tome12_page12.text: Listen to what I tell you! The Plague God will cleanse us from the weaknesses of mankind. No empire can be greater than nature. The Emperor is a puppet of the priests of Harat. The people will know this once the Plague God's blessings touch their hearts. The strong will become stronger and the weak... the weak are not meant to have children.
item.tome12_page13.text: The truth is that only we can stand against evil and injustice. Only we can create a better world atop the ruins that are the Empire's lies. Only we can stand against the Grim King, defeated in the forests of Lubenia by the Plague God's might. We have that weapon. And soon our time shall come.
item.tome12_page14.text: These Night Guests will never dare enter our abode. They can scare meek peasants, but they understand that they will receive a different welcome here. I know who created those spirits. The one whose evil cannot rest even in death. The one who had no right to life, no right to the throne, no right to say those prayers that should be forgotten forever.
item.tome13.name: Geographic Almanac of the Empire
item.tome13_page01.text: The Northern Lands, conquered in the War of the Grim King, were never properly settled. The distance from the capital and so many heretics and outlaws of every shade made it difficult to quickly tame. And with the rise of the Plaguelands, the idea of their development was put off until the present crisis passed.
item.tome13_page02.text: Like every frontier, the Northern Lands are inhabited by the dregs of society—mostly thieves and murderers. The last decade the empire lost all its control over the territory to the Gray Decay and hordes of barbarians trying to eke out a living along the Empire's deserted borders.
item.tome13_page03.text: Pagan cultures thrive wherever the Holy Faith can't duly oversee the populace. Human sacrifice, worship of false gods, and other unspeakable barbarities continue with impunity at the Empire's northern edges. One of the most heinous attestations of the people's sinfulness are living totems. Disfigured trees grown around human bodies that have turned into half-plant, half-undead persons.
item.tome13_page04.text: Among the Northern Lands most notable features are its unique and beautiful natural landscapes of bright birch trees and rolling hills. The lands are rich with resources, including iron that's perfect for crafting quality armor and weapons.
item.tome14.name: Lord Huginn's Notes
item.tome14_page01.text: The Empire celebrates a victory today — a victory in a war against a child. Wish I could say I was sorry, but there was no other way. Imbued with the power of the Nameless God — the power of death itself — he started to take all those who turned away from him. He was prophesied to take the throne, and with that would come the Empire's end. And yet, the Grim King fell. The Empire rejoices. So how come I don't feel at peace?
item.tome14_page02.text: People are going missing in the forests. Those few who manage to escape tell of dark, ghostly beings that whisper in an unknown tongue. They carry sickles in their hands, and their faces are nothing but a dark abyss. There's no doubt that the Nameless God is behind this. But that's for me to confirm.
item.tome14_page03.text: I saw him. I sent a scout on a fake mission into the forest and followed him. As soon as night fell, I heard a howl: the cries of a hundred perished souls merged into one being poured forth, begging for release from their torture. That phantom specter appeared from nowhere and in a second ended that poor scout's life — and then it turned to look at me. I recognized those eyes. The Grim King is returning. The Empire did not stop the prophecy from coming true. We just delayed the inevitable.
item.tome14_page04.text: I spent the next months in a temple library. We'll never defeat the Grim King on our own. He draws power from the Nameless God himself. But we still have a chance at victory. We will, however, have to rely on another god.
item.tome14_page05.text: We must do it. We will call upon the Plague God and release the Gray Decay upon this world. The Empire will declare a quarantine and strengthen the city defenses. Those touched by the plague cannot be taken by the Nameless God. That sacrifice will give us the time we need to summon our forces, to gather our strength. When the Grim King returns, when the Reaping Night falls — I will be ready!
item.tome14_page06.text: I found the Gatekeeper, obtained the key, and made it into the Forsaken Order's dungeon. Just as I thought, the Order has succumbed to the plague and is gathering strength. I fear, however, that Eisenborg plans to exact revenge upon the Empire, not go to war with the Grim King. I hope I can change his mind. The Master would make a powerful ally...
item.tome15.name: Aissa's Diary
item.tome15_page01.text: The council of the patriarchs has given me an important mission. I am to raise a boy, not just any boy, a son of the Emperor. No priestess has ever been accorded such high honor. I must do everything—anything—to justify the trust placed in me. May the Light guide me.
item.tome15_page02.text: The princes turned twelve today. The Emperor threw a grand feast to celebrate his heir's birthday. I was the only one to celebrate with his younger brother. And the little prince was so happy when he received the horse I carved for him. The Light sparkles in his eye. He may never inherit the throne, but I know that my boy is destined for greatness.
item.tome15_page03.text: Emperor Wilhelm is dead. The throne has passed to his oldest son, Ioann. I pray to the Light that the new Emperor inherited his father's wisdom and sense of justice. But something is happening in the palace. The High Priest has ordered me to be patient and warned me that I will soon have to carry out my duty. I don't know what he meant, but I will go to the ends of the earth for my boy.
item.tome15_page04.text: I went before the High Priest today. He commanded me to kill the boy. I'm still in shock. It goes against everything I was taught. What could that innocent child have done wrong? The priests fear the prophecy so much, but if they could only look into the little prince's eyes...
item.tome15_page05.text: In the name of the Light! We've fled. I smuggled the prince out of the palace. We'll go straight to the border, to the Lubenian forests. The guards will realize soon and come straight after us. We cannot use the main roads, and we'll have to hide our faces. No one can be trusted. I am all he has—and he is all I have, too.
item.tome15_page06.text: We were caught in the middle of a storm. The boy is wet to the bone. We had no choice but to stop in a village to wait out the rain. A local family let us sleep in their barn. They realized who we were but helped us despite the risk. The Imperial army, led by the priests of Harat, is on our tail. I can't think about what will happen if they catch us. I must keep the boy safe no matter the costs.
item.tome15_page07.text: They killed everyone. The peasants didn't give us up, so they were burned inside their homes. It's a miracle we escaped the barn and ran. The boy's face was burned. He has a fever. This is the Light they bring, those priests of Harat. The Light that was supposed to warm now burns the Empire's innocent victims. We cannot stop anywhere else and put others at risk.
item.tome15_page08.text: We ran for several days until we were lost in a dense thicket of dead trees. A flock of crows blocked out the sun and people dressed in black appeared from the fog. I knew who they were. Adepts of the god of death. It's as if they knew where to find us. And yet they didn't hurt us—at least not yet. I don't know what's in store for us now, but the prince needs to rest.
item.tome15_page09.text: My fears were unfounded. I understand now that the adepts are not the crazed heretics the priests warned me about. Quite the opposite, they welcomed us with open arms. They sheltered and fed us. They say our meeting was foreseen—and the prophecy must come true... Either way, we must remain in the camp until the prince gets better. They promised to defend us with their lives.
item.tome15_page10.text: The adepts turned out to have a great many books forbidden by the priests of Harat. They have scrolls that are hundreds, thousands of years old. How could I be so naïve? All this time I've been the victim of an evil lie, the servant of an unclean faith. I became blind after looking towards the Light for so long. And only in the dark can you find the shadow of the Truth. I now know everything they didn't want me to.
item.tome15_page11.text: Days go by, but the prince only gets worse. His fever is like a fire under his skin. I've argued with the adepts and screamed at them, but there's only one thing left to do. We have to do the ritual. I must accept the prophecy. I will accept the god of death and become the prince's mother in another life. Nothing will ever separate us again.
item.tome15_page12.text: Fear not, my son. I am here. They wanted you dead and you accepted death. Leave this world in peace, my little prince. Live, my Grim King.
item.tome16.name: Stranger's Riddles
item.tome16_page01.text: You've lived in these forsaken lands for some time now. But how well do you really know this place? I want to give you a little challenge. Figure out my riddles and receive a valuable reward. Let's start with something easy. Farmers, artisans, and shepherds... all used to live here. But where are they now? Find them — and you will find the next letter.
item.tome16_page02.text: Not bad, but that was just the start. As you know, as soon as the plague started, many tried to run, taking everything they could carry with them. Some made it to the border and, maybe, found a better place to settle. But for many, their journeys ended in tears. Can you find their trail?
item.tome16_page03.text: First, the Empire sent knights to battle the Plague. But it soon became evident that their strength wouldn't be enough. That's why they organized the militia. Their ranks were filled with no more than peasants who'd never held anything sharper than a sickle. Women were left alone at home, wondering if they'd ever see their husbands and sons again. When the news of their loved ones' deaths reached them, the sorrow was too great to handle and they resolved to desperate measures.
item.tome16_page04.text: You're halfway there. You've done well, solving my riddles, and deserve a small reward. Here's a map to find it.
item.tome16_page05.text: The Plague isn't the Empire's only problem. The trouble began much earlier, with the Great Evil. The adherents of that evil brought about great calamities and created a truly terrible enemy. Nonetheless, they left something useful to us in their wake. Something that can only be seen under the dark cover of night.
item.tome16_page06.text: When the great plague reached the city, the Empire sealed itself off behind massive walls, leaving its outskirts to their own fate. Anyone who came in contact with the sickness was immediately sentenced to death. One of the Orders fighting the epidemic was cruelly tricked into being infected. Despite the warriors' loyalty and their master's persuasiveness, the Order was immediately banished by the Empire. They were forced to seek a new refuge.
item.tome16_page07.text: The farmers turned into dead men walking. Knights turned from saviors into carriers of the all-consuming disease. Grieving widows found a new purpose in serving the Plague God. But criminals stayed true to their craft. Theft and murder were their lots before and after the spreading madness. You already know who I mean, don't you?
item.tome16_page08.text: You've almost reached your goal. There's just one last letter. I hid it near your home. Search for a lock without a key, where there is kept a key without a lock.
item.tome16_page09.text: You really are well-acquainted with the history of our destitute new world. Stopping the evil requires knowing from whence it came. I believe you are destined to defeat it. It will be a long and tiring battle, but today... today you may rest. Here are the coordinates with the last point of our short journey. I await you there.
item.tome17.name: Notes of the Captain of the Iron Wolves
item.tome17_page01.text: Our Order's mission is to find and destroy the heretical text that threatens the Empire. We've discovered the old citadel has fallen to the Mourning Reapers. There hasn't been any news about them in some time. That imperial order always made a terrible impression on me. Their odd rituals... Now I think they could have always served some other emperor with all their talk about prophecies and the afterlife.
item.tome17_page02.text: A terrible feeling ran through me as we walked under the cliff's shadow on our approach to the Citadel. But what we saw... The Mourning Reapers are gone, the castle is infested with the ghosts of their fallen knights. We managed to beat a few of them back, but they literally drained the life from us, and I had to sound the retreat. At least we found the haven of the Grim King's disciples. They now know our objective, and what we learned left us trembling.
item.tome17_page03.text: The disciples tell us that the Grim King stopped at the Citadel for a short time. Rogvold, the Reapers' leader, picked this place to make a willing sacrifice of himself and his knights. And the Nameless God accepted their offering. The citadel became sacred for the disciples, for it now simultaneously exists in our world and in Shobol. All the Order's knights were resurrected as evil shadows—wandering ghosts with no memory of their former selves.
item.tome17_page04.text: The shadows guard the boundary between the realm of the dead and the world of the living. When we again approached the Citadel, a flash of lightning revealed to us what Rogvold had become. It was terrifying. Nothing can save this eternally cursed land. Before dying, the disciples admitted they hid their heretical text, ciphering it multiple times in ways only they could unscramble. But solving riddles isn't a military duty—all that is left for us is to stop Rogvold and his army of shadows.
item.tome18.name: Master Karn's Notes
item.tome18_page01.text: We have killed for the glory of the Empire. And the Empire demanded more corpses. We spilled blood for the glory of the Empire. And the empire thirsted for more blood. And now that the Darkness is on the move in the north, we have been recalled to the capital. But who knows the north better than we do? I should have challenged this decision: our place is on the front lines. But the will of the Emperor is paramount.
item.tome18_page02.text: Rumors of disease are spreading around the capital. That's why they sent us here? Rumors? My troops are languishing from inaction behind stone walls! They're banned from the arena so the Emperor can protect his best fighters. Tomorrow Marcus is holding a feast for the masters and bragging about getting fine wine from Lubenia. I'd rather we held joint training sessions—then I'd show them how real men fight. Alas, we'll settle for wine for now.
item.tome18_page03.text: I don't remember the events of last night very well. The wine flowed like a river, but now I feel an incredible surge of power! My body is overflowing with energy that must be released. Marcus, what potion did you slip me? But never mind that. Thanks to you, I realized we're not the type to sit around in a kennel like dogs. In our veins flows the blood of barbarians whose only wish was to glimpse the mortal terror in the eyes of their enemies.
item.tome18_page04.text: We, the first order, have always been feared and envied, but now everyone is against us. And it's all because of some worthless priest. He was acting too high and mighty, and I was obliged to kill him. That sufficed for the Emperor to brand my order as traitors, and my former brothers from other orders, who had once broken bread with us, attacked my soldiers. We had to fight our way out of the capital that we had recently entered as heroes.
item.tome18_page05.text: They call me a madman. They say the voices made me kill. The voices told me to lead my Order to the ancient dungeon in the Plaguelands. They do not know what I know. They do not know what we faced in the North. The voices just opened my eyes to the truth. The Empire of the Light made us pawns in a war that was lost long ago. But the War Dogs will not follow suit.
item.tome18_page06.text: We drank blood. We swore an oath. Ancient words to rouse a hidden power—he whispered them to me. He reminded me. He returned what is rightfully mine. My fighters—they tore, hacked, mangled. I was in the heat of the battle, but fury no longer clouded my mind. The voices became a song. They sing of my exaltation. We are no longer dogs. We no longer have an owner. From now on, we will call ourselves the Torturers, for from torture we derive joy.
item.tome18_page07.text: The sentinels shot a messenger from the Crows. On his body they found a letter bearing Huginn's seal. The cunning Crow says the Emperor has sent the Lions and Riders for our heads. Let them come. These two orders will be a great warm-up for my fighters. We'll take their lives. Perhaps we will even allow their hardiest soldiers to join our ranks.
item.tome18_page08.text: The Crow once again spoiled the fun. His people meddled in our battle and allowed the survivors from the Lions and Riders to escape. Huginn tried to convince me that we are allies and must carry the Plague God's will into this world. Well, let him keep thinking that. People like the Crow always need someone to serve. When the time comes, I'll pluck every last feather from that cowardly bird!
item.tome18_page09.text: Marcus, my old friend, has beckoned me to join him in his search for the Grim King. He wants to fight against the Darkness in the name of his new master. But why? This dungeon contains everything my heart desires. Thousands of captives scream in hopeless attempts to make it out alive, and rivers of blood flow in the torture chambers. And with every drop of blood, my warriors grow even stronger! Soon all kings will bow before my might!
item.tome18_page10.text: A new campaign draws near. An endless campaign. We will gather our forces in the north and deal a crushing blow to the Empire. The voices have sent us allies. Barbarian hunters have appeared in our camp, led by a young priestess. She says that their God desires to help us. That soon, others will come who will fight under my command. "We all serve His will," she says. I want to kill her, but the voices command me to stop. I will let her live. For now.
item.tome18_page11.text: The barbarians are becoming more tiresome and erratic. Their head priest kept claiming that I had not dedicated myself thoroughly to serving God. Well, I have shown my loyalty. By torturing the priest to death in the ritual circle. His agony only multiplied my power. The same will happen to any who demand that we serve.
item.tome18_page12.text:
The Emperor. Light. Gods. They're all waiting for us to bend the knee. To become their silent weapon. They believe they can subdue us. Break us. Give us orders. But they no longer cloud my mind. Nothing, not even death, can stop people in whose veins flows true power. Any who try to get in our way face a fate worse than death.
We will not be worthless Dogs. 
We shall strip away the flesh of the doomed world. 
We shall rejoice in its agony.
We are Torturers!
item.tome19.name: Researcher's Journal
item.tome19_page01.text:
The scrolls I bought from a knight were found in the ruins of the Scarlet Angels' library. They seem to resemble historical chronicles written long before the Empire's founding. The Angels copied them but couldn't translate the ancient tongue. I understand some phrases, but a full translation will take time.
The chronicles mostly concern the building of a temple. "Crimson sandstone walls stretch skyward." I wonder if it is still around today.
item.tome19_page02.text:
The temple of crimson sandstone is described as either a "burial place" or "place of awakening." It is hard to tell without context. I am still working on the translation, but I only have fragments. 
I had to use my influence to obtain an audience with the curator of the Imperial Library. Perhaps if I compare the scrolls to contemporary texts, I will be able to piece together the whole picture.
item.tome19_page03.text:
All I managed to save was this journal and map. The other records and books have likely already been burned. What happened to the Empire to make history equivalent to heresy?
My title spared me from the fire. But the church won't take long to find a way to deal with a woman who knows more than she should. I ran to the Plaguelands, where, among the forests, the crimson temple ought to be. My life may be ruined, but my work is still unfinished.
item.tome19_page04.text:
I have no doubt that this is the place described in the ancient texts. But all I found were ruins of gray stone blocks.
It is as if these ruins attract the leprous and damned. I must find a safe place before dark. I saw a staircase that led down to a basement or dungeon. I could wait out the night there behind solid doors and continue my search in the morning. At the moment, I can't even consider the idea that my trip has been in vain.
item.tome19_page05.text:
I can't believe it. When I went down the stairs, I expected to see catacombs or a godforsaken tomb. But these are the halls of the temple that I read about. Crimson columns, inscriptions on the walls...
I made an error in my translation: the temple stretches not skyward, but into the depths. That is why it stayed hidden for centuries!
I will write down everything I learn. Maybe in better times my notes will help restore the history that was burned.
item.tome19_page06.text: If there was once a library here, its scrolls turned to dust long ago. But there are still carvings on the walls, and the symbols clearly predate the ones used by the pagan cults. And I also glimpse similarities to Harat's sacred symbols. Is this the knowledge that the church tried to burn?
item.tome19_page07.text:
The symbols repeat on each floor. I have copied all of them, but they are practically impossible to decipher without any books at hand. Some are similar to symbols of protection or talismans. It seems they are meant to protect against outsiders. Or are they supposed to restrain something?
I can hear the echo of steps in the hallways and the clank of iron. Someone else has found this place.
item.tome19_page08.text:
A battle is going on up above. I managed to make out the insignia of the fallen orders: the Forsaken and the Torturers, as they're now called. I think I also saw someone from the Black Crows. Perhaps others will come soon too.
The temple seems to have awoken and is calling its servants.
My way out has been cut off. All I can do is keep going down. If I have translated the signs correctly, the lower floors should house a sanctuary.
item.tome19_page09.text:
My torch died out a long time ago. But the inscriptions on the walls glow with a dim crimson light. They pulse with warmth. They whisper. They summon me downward.
